strategies.name: Scale-in momentum + 50-day exit
strategies.plain: Buys crypto only while it has been rising, and steps aside when the short trend breaks.
strategies.universe: Forward basket: BTC, ETH, XRP, BNB, SOL. Daily bars.
strategies.hypothesis: Crypto trends persist across a few horizons. A close below the 50-day average is meant to cut off the deep bear markets that make holding painful. The 200-day average is meant to keep the book out of an established downtrend.
rules: Target exposure is one third for each of the 30-, 90-, and 180-day returns that is positive, and only while the close is above the 200-day average.
A daily close below the 50-day average goes to cash. Re-entry needs a fresh 20-day closing high, and the momentum and 200-day filters still have to allow exposure.
Forward basket: up to one fifth of equity per coin, times that target fraction. Rebalance only when the target level changes.
Cost on the research note: 0.10% per side. A doubled-fee check was also run on the backtest.
strategies.backtest: In-sample BTC backtest, Nov 1, 2021 to Nov 4, 2026: +203.4%, maximum drawdown −21.7%, against buy-and-hold +31.7% and −76.6%. Doubled fees: +189.8%. The 2025–26 window had already been looked at, so it is not a clean holdout. That path is not drawn here.
strategies.forward: $10,000, 100% cash through the Nov 8 close. Every coin was in the 50-day lockout. The forward test has not proven anything yet.
strategies.risk: Whipsaw around the 50-day line, and a three-week window that is too short to judge.

why.text: The first BTC runs that led to this pick (Nov 4, 2026) printed +223% with a −20% worst drop for scale-in + 50-day exit, but they saved only console output, so that figure was withdrawn as unverifiable. The saved re-run (new experiment, Nov 5, next-day fills, 0.10% fees): Nov 1, 2021 to Nov 4, 2026, +203.4% with a −21.7% maximum drawdown, against BTC buy-and-hold +31.7% and −76.6%; doubled fees +189.8%. Same re-run, five-coin basket with the 50-day exit: +128.2% (−36.1%), and +16.1% (−12.3%) for Jan 2025 to Nov 4, 2026. Separate Nov 5 comparison, three coins (BTC/ETH/SOL), Jan 1, 2025 to Nov 4, 2026, next-open fills: +21.05%, maximum drawdown −14.53%, 16 trades. All in-sample; the 2025–26 window had already been looked at.

strategies.name: Crypto z-score mean reversion
strategies.plain: Buys a coin after a sharp dip, looking for a bounce back toward its recent average.
strategies.universe: Ten large-cap coins, daily: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, ADA, AVAX, LINK, LTC.
strategies.hypothesis: Sharp selloffs of about one standard deviation in liquid coins tend to retrace part of the way toward the 30-day mean.
rules: z = (close − 30-day mean) / 30-day sample standard deviation, including the signal day.
Buy when z crosses from at or above −1 to below −1. Fill at the next UTC day's open. Deepest z first.
Exit at the next open once a close has z at or above 0. Stop: −15% on a close, filled at that close. Time stop: 20 days.
$1,000 per position including the fee, maximum 10 positions. Cost 0.10% per side.
strategies.backtest: No backtest of these exact rules. A different 20-day / −1.5σ variant is context only and is not drawn here.
strategies.forward: $9,871.20 (−1.29%). 9 positions open, 0 closed. BTC bought at the Nov 5 open: $9,254.30 (−7.46%).
strategies.risk: In a trending selloff the signals cluster, so ten positions can act like one large long-crypto bet. A close-only stop can lose more than 15% on a gap.

why.text: No saved backtest of these exact rules (30-day z-score, enter below −1, $1,000 slots, −15% stop, 20-day max hold) exists in the records. The closest record is a different variant (20-day z-score, enter below −1.5, 200-day filter) in the Nov 5 comparison: BTC, Mar 1, 2021 to Nov 4, 2026, +20.22% with a −11.78% maximum drawdown, 28 trades, 78.6% winners; BTC/ETH/SOL +29.39% (−10.50%). That is context only, not a test of this account's rules.

strategies.name: Crypto Bollinger band reversion
strategies.plain: Same dip idea, using a band around the average instead of a z-score.
strategies.universe: The same ten coins as the z-score book, daily. Run as its own account.
strategies.hypothesis: The same overreaction idea as the z-score book, with a volatility band as the trigger. The comparison asks whether the trigger matters.
rules: Middle band is the 20-day mean. Lower band is the middle minus 2 population standard deviations, including that day's close.
Signal when the completed bar's low touches the lower band, or the close is below it, and the coin is not already held.
Exit when a completed close is back at or above the middle band. −15% close stop. 20-day maximum hold.
$1,000 per position including the fee, maximum 10. Cost 0.10% per side.
strategies.risk: The low-touch trigger fills the book faster in a selloff, so the same correlated drawdown shows up sooner.

why.text: No original backtest record exists for this strategy. It was launched as a forward-only paper test, run next to the z-score test so the two dip-buying rules can be compared on the same dates.

strategies.name: EMA 13/80 crossover
strategies.plain: Holds a coin only while a fast average sits above a slow one.
strategies.universe: BTC, ETH, SOL. Forward test on daily bars. A 4-hour backtest was also run.
strategies.hypothesis: A classic moving-average filter for medium-term crypto trends. Long only. The source post also shorted; that side was left out.
rules: Long an asset while its 13-day EMA is above its 80-day EMA. Otherwise flat.
Signal at the close, filled at the next close.
One third of equity per asset when long. The rest stays in cash. Trade only when the target changes.
0.10% fee plus 0.10% slippage per side.
strategies.backtest: In-sample daily test, Nov 1, 2021 to Nov 5, 2026: +45.12%, maximum drawdown −55.19%, against BTC buy-and-hold +24.92%. The 2025–26 slice was −1.07%. That path is not drawn here.
strategies.forward: $9,987.70, in cash. One closed trade so far, a small loss. No forward buy-and-hold dollar figure was stated.
strategies.risk: The backtest drawdown, about −55%, is deeper than most people would sit through. The average lags turns.

why.text: Taken from a Reddit post (r/CryptoTradingBot). Saved baseline, Nov 1, 2021 to Nov 5, 2026, BTC/ETH/SOL daily, next-close fills, 0.10% fee plus 0.10% slippage per side: +45.12% with a −55.19% maximum drawdown, 198 trades, against BTC buy-and-hold +24.92%. Jan 2025 onward: −1.07% against −19.56%. In-sample, and the drawdown is far past the 10% limit.

strategies.name: 30-day breakout
strategies.plain: Buys a coin that closes at a 30-day high, and sells when it falls under its 30-day average.
strategies.universe: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE. Daily.
strategies.hypothesis: New highs can keep going as later buyers and short-covering push price up. This is a control taken from a public Bot Wars post.
rules: Enter or hold when the close is above the prior 30-day high. Today's close is not part of that high.
Exit when the close drops below the 30-day average close. No separate stop.
Equal weight across the coins that qualify. Cash if none qualify.
0.10% fee plus 0.10% slippage per side. Signal at the close, filled at the next close.
strategies.backtest: In-sample, Nov 1, 2021 to Nov 5, 2026: +118.77%, maximum drawdown −47.8%, about $5,055 in fees. 2025–26: +2.67%. That path is not drawn here.
strategies.forward: $10,000.00, flat. No coin has broken out since launch.
strategies.risk: High turnover. In the five-year backtest, fees were about half the starting capital. Ranges produce many false breakouts.

why.text: Taken from an X post (@ainotesus, "Bot Wars"). Saved baseline, Nov 1, 2021 to Nov 5, 2026, five coins: +118.77% with a −47.8% maximum drawdown, 530 trades and about $5,055 in fees, against BTC buy-and-hold +24.92%. Jan 2025 onward: +2.67% against −19.56%. In-sample.

strategies.name: Halving 500
strategies.plain: Owns bitcoin for 500 days before and after a halving. Cash the rest of the time. Still waiting to buy.
strategies.window: Waiting for a frozen buy on Dec 14, 2026. Hold would run toward Sep 9, 2029.
strategies.hypothesis: Bitcoin's issuance cuts line up with a rough four-year boom and bust. Being in cash during the late bear is meant to avoid the worst of it.
rules: Hold 100% BTC from 500 calendar days before a halving until 500 days after. Cash otherwise.
The next buy date is frozen at Dec 14, 2026, and the sell date at Sep 9, 2029, so the signal does not drift every day.
Fill at the next daily close. 0.10% fee plus 0.10% slippage per side.
strategies.backtest: Three testable cycles versus buy-and-hold, all in-sample: 2015–17 +3,377% vs +3,285%; 2018–21 +1,017% (drawdown −61.8%) vs +989%; 2022–25 +546% vs +557%. Those paths are not drawn here. Only about three cycles can be tested.
strategies.forward: $10,000.00, cash, waiting for Dec 14, 2026. Nothing has been bought.
strategies.risk: A tiny sample, a chart that was drawn with hindsight, and an edge over buy-and-hold that was small in two of the three cycles.

why.text: Taken from a viral X chart (hold BTC from 500 days before each halving to 500 days after). Saved baseline, per cycle versus buy-and-hold: 2015–17 +3,377% vs +3,285%; 2018–21 +1,017% (drawdown −61.8%) vs +989%; 2022–25 +546% (−28.1%) vs +557%. A fresh $10,000 from Nov 1, 2021: +545.7% with a −28.14% maximum drawdown vs BTC +31.8%. Only about three cycles, and the chart was drawn in hindsight.

strategies.name: SEASONS
strategies.plain: A four-season cycle for bitcoin. The rules are still being built, so there is no account yet.
strategies.window: 12 months of tracking once it is live. No start date yet.
strategies.hypothesis: Price-confirmed seasons (a new all-time high, a 30% break, then capitulation and recovery) might time the cycle better than a fixed 500-day offset.
rules: Spring starts at the halving. Summer starts on the first close above the prior cycle's all-time high.
Fall starts on a 30% drop from the summer high. The account is in cash during fall.
Winter starts after 300 or more days of fall, a drawdown of 60% or more, and a close above the 50-day average.
Exposure for each non-fall phase is still to be frozen before launch. Cost plan: 0.10% fee plus 0.10% slippage per side.
strategies.backtest: Not yet backtested. The rules are still being built.
strategies.forward: Not launched. No paper account, no marks, no curve.
strategies.risk: About four halvings of history, phase rules that can be read more than one way, and a framework published after much of the history it describes.

why.text: Picked from Jeff Terpin's "Four Seasons" halving-cycle book as a rule set worth tracking. No backtest record exists yet; the rules are still being built, so there is no number to show.

strategies.name: S&P 500 dip-buy
strategies.plain: Buys large stocks that have fallen at least 20% under their short average.
strategies.hypothesis: Panic selling can push large-cap stocks too far below a short trend, and part of that gap can close.
rules: Signal when a stock's close is at least 20% below its 25-day average. The average includes today's close. Deepest discount first.
Buy at the next session's open. Exit at the next open after a close back at or above the 25-day average.
Stop: −15% on a close versus entry, filled at that close. Time stop: 20 trading days.
$1,000 per position. Up to 10 slots. Cost 0.05% per side.
strategies.forward: $9,212.25 (−7.88%) against SPY $9,865.00 (−1.35%). Four closed trades, all stop-outs (MRVL, LITE, TER, SNDK on Nov 5), about −$850 together. 9 positions were still open. Win rate on closed trades: 0%.
strategies.risk: A stock down 20% is often down for a reason. Close-only stops can be blown through by a gap, which is what those four exits did.

why.text: No original backtest of this equity rule (close 20% below the 25-day average, $1,000 slots, −15% stop, 20-day max hold) exists in the records. The only related record is a different market: a crypto dip-buy grid on the quant desk (Nov 4, 2026, 32 coins pooled), whose 200-day-filtered form had a −32% maximum drawdown and a deflated Sharpe of −0.64, which breaks the 10% limit. That is not a test of this account's rules.

strategies.name: Nasdaq top-5 momentum
strategies.plain: Each month, holds the five Nasdaq-100 stocks that rose the most over the prior six months.
strategies.universe: Current Nasdaq-100 members with enough history. Monthly rebalance.
strategies.hypothesis: Recent relative winners tend to keep outperforming for a while. Five names, equal weight.
rules: At each month-end close, rank by the trailing 126 trading days and hold the top 5, 20% each.
Names that drop out are sold. Fill at the next trading day's close.
The 126-day lookback is the note's assumption. The source post did not specify it.
Cost 0.10% per side. Benchmark is QQQ. No forward QQQ dollar figure was stated.
strategies.backtest: In-sample, Nov 2021 to Nov 4, 2026: +749.13%, maximum drawdown −38.67%, against QQQ +84.02%. The note says not to trust that number: today's index members are used, so removed losers are missing. That path is not drawn here.
strategies.forward: $10,239.95 (+2.40%) as of the Nov 6 close. Holds PANW, MU, CRWD, DDOG, and MRNA from the Oct 30 ranking.
strategies.risk: Five concentrated, mostly high-beta names. Momentum can reverse hard at a turn. The backtest is inflated by survivorship bias.

why.text: Taken from an X post (@QuantifiedStrat). Saved baseline, Nov 2021 to Nov 4, 2026: +749.13% with a −38.67% maximum drawdown, 345 trades, against QQQ +84.02%; Jan 2025 onward +274.85% vs +36.77%. Do not trust that number: it uses today's Nasdaq-100 members, so companies that fell out of the index are missing (survivorship bias), and the 126-day lookback is our assumption because the post did not say.

strategies.name: 9 EMA + VWAP intraday
strategies.plain: A day-trade that buys a small dip while price is above the day's average, and is flat by the close.
strategies.universe: SPY and QQQ, 5-minute bars. $10,000 split into two $5,000 sleeves.
strategies.sleeveNote: The note states day-1 percents, not sleeve dollar balances. The dots are $5,000 times those percents.

benchmark.name: 50/50 buy-and-hold, day-1 percent
benchmark.note: +1.93% on day 1. Not drawn on this sleeve scale.

strategies.hypothesis: A widely shared day-trading setup: buy a pullback to a short average while price is above VWAP. The test asks whether it survives once the rules and costs are written down.
rules: Primary entry: the previous close is above both VWAP and the 9-bar EMA, the EMA is rising, the bar's low touches the EMA, and the close finishes above both. Not the first or last bar of the session.
Enter at the next bar's open. Stop at VWAP minus one cent, checked first. Otherwise exit after a close below the EMA, or at the session's last close. Flat overnight.
Variant: enter when the close reclaims both EMA and VWAP. Same exit, no stop. Reported separately.
Each trade uses the full sleeve. Cost 0.03% per side. A 0.06% sensitivity run was also done on the backtest.
strategies.backtest: Aug 17 to Nov 6, 2026, 59 sessions, in-sample: primary −9.79%, variant −14.37%, against 50/50 buy-and-hold −7.87%. That path is not drawn here.
strategies.forward: Day 1 only (Nov 9): primary −0.18%, variant +0.18%, buy-and-hold +1.93%. A combined dollar balance was not stated.
strategies.risk: Many trades and a low win rate. Small costs add up. The stop is checked on 5-minute bars; the source used 1-minute bars.

why.text: Picked to check a popular YouTube/blog day-trading claim, not because the backtest looked good. Saved baseline, Aug 17 to Nov 6, 2026 (59 sessions), 5-minute bars, 0.03% cost per side: SPY primary −8.91% (153 trades, 13.7% winners) vs buy-and-hold −5.26%; QQQ primary −10.66% (172 trades) vs −10.47%. At 0.06% per side the losses roughly double. In-sample and short.
